source.title: Training Matching Pursuit SAEs on LLMs

record.file_problem: The post is present in full, but referenced charts and their numerical values are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The post evaluates sparse-probing performance of SAEs trained on an LLM, bearing on the LLM-specific indirect-evidence version; it does not test the toy-model geometry directly.
record.gate_note: The post reports that all MP-SAEs score worse than traditional SAEs on k-sparse probing at k=1 and k=16, and that MP-SAEs perform worse on the feature-absorption metric. Referenced charts are absent from the supplied text, so only the stated comparisons can be recorded. Training-time, reconstruction, and decoder-norm results are omitted because they do not directly test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post trains matching-pursuit SAEs on Gemma-2-2b layer 12 and compares them with BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs on reconstruction, k-sparse probing and absorption. It reports only how SAE architectures perform relative to each other. It treats SAE recovery of sparse features as a working tool and does not test whether superposition or recoverable sparse features exist. No result bears on any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the author expected MP-SAEs to reduce absorption, as the MP-SAE paper implies, and found the opposite. The author speculates that absorption is a degenerate route to better reconstruction.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains and evaluates matching-pursuit and traditional SAEs on an LLM; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The post compares MP-SAEs at L0≈85 and L0≈265, including a static L0=85 variant, but the supplied text does not give chart values by individual SAE or L0.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-2b layer 12, MP-SAEs reconstruct better than BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs at matched L0, but score notably worse on k=1 and k=16 sparse probing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Better SAE reconstruction at fixed L0 need not mean better recovery of the model's features; MP-SAEs may find degenerate solutions.

fits_no_version.finding: MP-SAEs score much worse than traditional SAEs on the SAEBench absorption metric; Matryoshka SAEs score best.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching-pursuit encoders do not reduce feature absorption in an LLM, contrary to the MP-SAE paper's motivation.

record.problems: The author calls the analysis non-rigorous and reports results from only a few SAEs trained on Gemma-2-2b. The supplied text omits the referenced charts and numerical results, and the post says SCR and TPP evaluations were not practical to run.
record.rows_left_out: Training-time, reconstruction, decoder-norm, and dead-latent observations were not extracted as rows because they do not directly measure a claim version. SCR and TPP results are not reported; the author says the evaluations were too slow to run practically.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
All: no test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
All: no test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or are sparse features a dictionary recovers. Only relative SAE-architecture quality is reported.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. The author did not compare what MP-SAEs and traditional SAEs learn.
All: feature manifolds are mentioned only as future work.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests' with tranche T3 and its V4 limits_scope label are removed. Comparing SAE architectures is the study's own method against others, not evidence on whether superposition or sparse features hold in LLMs. All numeric results are in charts missing from the text.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or importance-dependent allocation.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The post evaluates SAE sparse-probing performance, but does not test whether features are spread across many neurons or directly establish that LLM features are sparse.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.
